chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'la, from Abu Makhlad al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who called another 'son of the insane'. So the other one said to him, 'You are a son of the insane'. So he (peace be upon him) ordered the first one to whip his companion with twenty lashes, and said to him, 'Know that he is also deserving the like of it, twenty'. So when he had whipped him, he (peace be upon him) gave the whip to the whipped one, so he whipped him, as a lesson to be learnt by both of them.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.ابْنُ الْمَجْنُونِ: Son of the insane (a specific type of accusation)
key_terms.دَعَا: Called / Accused (in the context of defamation)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on defamation and the penalty for falsely accusing someone?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the discretionary penalty (*ta'zir*) for defamation, where Ali (AS) ordered the accuser to receive twenty lashes for his false claim and the accused to receive twenty lashes for his reciprocal insult. This mutual punishment highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *nukl* (deterrence through exemplary punishment), ensuring that both parties are held equally accountable for disrupting social harmony through verbal abuse.
